newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris train blast kills two, wounds 28.
newsitem.headline: Paris train blast kills two, wounds 28.

text.p: Two people were killed and 28 injured, eight of them seriously, when an explosion rocked a station of the regional express underground railway in Paris on Tuesday, officials said.
The blast occurred in a carriage of the RER train at 6.05 p.m. (1705 GMT) at the Port Royal station on the Left Bank, the RATP transport authority said.
The cause of the explosion was not immediately known but investigators said it may have been caused by a bomb.
"There are apparently two dead," Prime Minister Alain Juppe told reporters before leaving his office for the scene of the blast.
The fire brigade said 28 people were injured, eight of them seriously in the blast below the junction of Boulevard Montparnasse and Boulevard Saint-Michel.
"We heard a strong blast," one witness who was in a bus above the station told France-Info radio.
"There was a column of black smoke which enveloped the bus. There was a strong smell of powder, like at a shooting range," she said.

The blast occurred on the same B line, and two stations away from Saint-Michel station where a blast in July last year killed eight people and injured nearly 100, launching a wave of attacks across France by Algerian Moslem fundamentalists.
Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre, as well as Paris anti-terrorism investigating magistrates travelled to the scene.
